references.text: God's promise to Abraham to make his descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky, which is the basis for the Lord's blessing mentioned in Deuteronomy 1:11
God's promise to multiply Abraham's offspring like the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore, a fulfillment of the blessing Moses refers to
God's promise to Isaac to make his descendants as numerous as the stars, part of the covenant promises that Moses points back to
God's promise to Jacob that his offspring will be like the dust of the earth, a continuation of the blessing promises given to the fathers
Moses reminds God of the promises to Abraham, Isaac, and Israel to multiply their descendants, the same promise tradition found in Deuteronomy 1:11
The Aaronic blessing that expresses the Lord's blessing over Israel, parallel to the theme of blessing in Deuteronomy 1:11
The Lord promises to bless and multiply Israel, a repetition of the blessing theme from Deuteronomy 1:11
The Lord rejoiced in making Israel numerous and blessing them, the fulfillment of the promise mentioned in Deuteronomy 1:11
David's prayer that the Lord would bless his house forever, the same theme of blessing as in Deuteronomy 1:11
Reference to God's promise to make Israel as numerous as the stars, a fulfillment of the promise Moses refers to
